text.p: America Online Inc. said Monday it has surpassed the 750,000 member mark outside of the United States, a year-and-a-half after launching its first international service.

The company said AOL Europe, a joint venture between America Online and Germany's Bertelsmann AG, has just passed 600,000 members. AOL Canada has grown to more than 100,000 members since it started in January 1996.

It said AOL Japan, the company's newest international service, launched on April 15, is "off to a fast start" but gave no figures. The operation is a partnership with Mitsui & Co. Ltd. and publisher Nihon Keizai Shimbun Inc., or Nikkei.
"This keeps us on track to hit our goal of 1 million non-U.S. members by this fall," said Jack Davies, president of AOL International.
AOL, based in Dulles, Va., estimates that it has about eight million subscribers, including its base of users in the United States.
AOL's stock rose $1 to $59.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
